card.name: Word just before a negative consequence
card.fires_on: Words in a condition or warning clause, such as 'too', 'improper', 'less' or 'if you', right before the text says what goes wrong. It covers the excess or faulty word itself, in both instructions and general advice.

modes.label: Too much or too little
modes.description: A word of excess or shortfall like too, less or far, which leads into a bad outcome.
modes.example: Introducing<< too>> much at one time will only frustrate

modes.label: Faulty-condition clause in instructions
modes.description: A word in a conditional or reason clause in handling or preparation steps, which leads into a warning.
modes.example: Follow the preparation instructions provided below, as<< improper>> preparation may lead to improper dose.

modes.label: If-clause conditions
modes.description: A small linking word inside an if-clause or a restriction, before the result is stated.
modes.example: You can't learn how to write if<< you>> simply download your papers from the Internet.
